…ob, not the CRLF working tree

The promote/verify gate read index.html from disk for its expected stamp, so a
Windows checkout (core.autocrlf=true, text=auto) turned the committed LF blob
into CRLF and that stamp no longer matched what main built and what staging
serves. The parity path already read each file from disk, which is correct for
those (they are compared after line-ending normalization), but the stamp is a
verbatim-signal check, not a normalized comparison.

Read git show :index.html for the expected stamp so both sides are the exact
committed bytes regardless of the checkout's line-ending representation.

commits.messageBody:
…he stamp from the committed blob

The promote/verify gate spawns verify-staging.mjs from a test working dir that
is not the repo root. Without a ROOT constant, path-relative reads (readFileSync
and execFileSync git show) hit the wrong tree, producing "ROOT is not defined"
crashes and stale-while-dirty verdicts. This commit:

- Adds ROOT = resolve(fileURLToPath(import.meta.url), "..") using ES-module-
  correct import.meta.url (not __dirname, which is not available in ES modules
  and caused an ERR_AMBIGUOUS_MODULE_SYNTAX crash on Node 24).
- Derives the expected stamp from git show :index.html (the committed blob)
  instead of readFileSync("index.html") (the working tree), so the stamp check
  is immune to checkout line-ending representation (CRLF vs LF) and to the
  spawn's CWD.
- Roots the parity path's git show :file reads at ROOT as well.

The working tree is LF-normalized (the file was CRLF in the repo; od confirms
0 CR characters after normalization) so git diff -- index.html-style checks
against the committed blob are honest.

commits.messageBody:
…tier)

Move only the `test` job in .github/workflows/test.yml from
`ubuntu-latest` to `runs-on: blacksmith-2vcpu-ubuntu-2404`, which is
Blacksmith's documented drop-in label for `ubuntu-latest` on Ubuntu
24.04 (2 vCPU / 8 GB / 80 GB).

Scope the pilot to one job, not the whole suite, because the free tier
is 3,000 x64 2-vCPU-equivalent minutes/month per organization and a
2-vCPU runner burns 1 allowance minute per clock minute. The `test`
job's 30-minute timeout means worst-case pilot burn is <=30
allowance-min per run; all other jobs stay on `ubuntu-latest` until
the pilot shows the actual burn and speedup. Larger Blacksmith sizes
(4/8/16/32 vCPU) burn the free allowance proportionally faster and
are not needed for this job.

This is a label-only change: Blacksmith's quickstart documents no
required workflow action or runner-registration step for the basic
Linux case. The one precondition that decides whether it boots vs
queues forever is org-side: the Blacksmith GitHub App must already
have access to this repository (org install with "All repositories",
or "Only select repositories" with this repo added). If the app does
not have access to this repo, the `test` job will queue instead of
run.
